_note: A DEMONSTRATION OF THE FORMAT, not the author's file. The real one is data/cast_types.json and is his. This exists so tools/cast_type_test.py can be run and read before that file is written; it names one real roster key only because the counts have to land on real turns to mean anything. Nothing at runtime reads either file.
_format: <roster key>: type (four letters) + axes.<EI|SN|TF|JP>.behaviour (one line of what the type was translated into) + axes.<axis>.markers.<pole> (observable markers: a Japanese surface form counted as a substring of the turn, or one of the structural facts named in tools/cast_type_test.py STRUCTURAL).

EI.behaviour: she opens rooms and fills silences instead of waiting to be addressed, and her messages come in bursts

E: sends more than one message in a row

SN.behaviour: she talks about what is in front of her -- the time, the place, the thing she is holding -- rather than what it might mean

TF.behaviour: she settles a thing rather than sitting with how somebody feels about it

JP.behaviour: she closes an open plan on the spot, with a time on it
